title: IIT JAM 2027 Physics (PH) — Full Length Mock Test 06
titleEn: IIT JAM 2027 Physics (PH) — Full Length Mock Test 06

questions.questionTextEn: A DC voltage source of emf $\mathcal{E}$ and internal resistance $r$ is connected to a variable load resistor $R_L$. The maximum power delivered to $R_L$ is
questions.explanationEn: Power delivered to $R_L$ is $P = \frac{\mathcal{E}^2 R_L}{(R_L + r)^2}$, which is maximized when $R_L = r$, giving $P_{\max} = \frac{\mathcal{E}^2 r}{(2r)^2} = \frac{\mathcal{E}^2}{4r}$.

questions.questionTextEn: For a plane electromagnetic wave propagating in vacuum, the ratio of the electric field amplitude $E_0$ to the magnetic field intensity amplitude $H_0 = B_0 / \mu_0$ is the intrinsic impedance of free space $\eta_0 = \sqrt{\frac{\mu_0}{\varepsilon_0}}$, whose value is approximately
questions.explanationEn: Using $\mu_0 = 4\pi\times 10^{-7}\text{ H/m}$ and $c \approx 3\times 10^8\text{ m/s}$, $\eta_0 = \mu_0 c \approx 120\pi\ \Omega \approx 377\ \Omega$.

questions.questionTextEn: A siren emitting sound of frequency $f_0$ moves directly away from a stationary listener at speed $v_s = c_s / 4$, where $c_s$ is the speed of sound in still air. The frequency heard by the listener is
questions.explanationEn: For a source receding at speed $v_s$ from a stationary observer, $f = f_0 \frac{c_s}{c_s + v_s} = f_0 \frac{1}{1 + 1/4} = \frac{4}{5}f_0$.

questions.questionTextEn: For an ideal gas in three dimensions, the pressure $P$ is related to the translational kinetic energy density $u_{\text{tr}}$ (translational kinetic energy per unit volume) by:
questions.explanationEn: From kinetic theory, $P = \frac{1}{3} n m \langle v^2 \rangle = \frac{2}{3} n \left(\frac{1}{2} m \langle v^2 \rangle\right) = \frac{2}{3} u_{\text{tr}}$. Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: A linear operator $\hat{A}$ representing a physical observable in quantum mechanics must be Hermitian ($\hat{A}^\dagger = \hat{A}$). Which of the following operators is Hermitian?
questions.explanationEn: Since $\hat{p}_x = -i\hbar\frac{d}{dx}$ is Hermitian, dividing by $-\hbar$ shows that $i\frac{d}{dx}$ is Hermitian (whereas $\frac{d}{dx}$ and $ix$ are anti-Hermitian, and $(x\frac{d}{dx})^\dagger = -\frac{d}{dx}x = -1 - x\frac{d}{dx}$ is not Hermitian). Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: For a bipolar junction transistor (BJT) operating in the active region, if $\alpha = I_C / I_E$ is the common-base DC current gain and $\beta = I_C / I_B$ is the common-emitter DC current gain, then $\alpha$ in terms of $\beta$ is:
questions.explanationEn: Using $I_E = I_B + I_C$ and $I_C = \beta I_B$, we obtain $I_E = (\beta + 1)I_B$. Therefore, $\alpha = \frac{I_C}{I_E} = \frac{\beta I_B}{(\beta + 1)I_B} = \frac{\beta}{\beta + 1}$. Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.questionTextEn: Converting the unsigned base-$10$ integer $413$ into hexadecimal (base-$16$) notation yields:
questions.explanationEn: Repeatedly divide $413$ by $16$: $413 = 16 \times 25 + 13$ (remainder $13 = \text{D}$); $25 = 16 \times 1 + 9$ (remainder $9$); $1 = 16 \times 0 + 1$ (remainder $1$). Reading remainders from bottom to top gives $(19\text{D})_{16}$. Check: $1 \times 256 + 9 \times 16 + 13 = 256 + 144 + 13 = 413$. Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.questionTextEn: For the real symmetric matrix $A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \end{pmatrix}$, what is the value of $\det(A)$?
questions.explanationEn: Expanding along the second row gives $\det(A) = 3 \begin{vmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{vmatrix} = 3(4 - 1) = 9$. Hence, option (D) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Two blocks of masses $2\text{ kg}$ and $6\text{ kg}$ are connected by a light inextensible string passing over a smooth massless pulley. When released from rest, the tension in the string is ($g$ is the acceleration due to gravity)
questions.explanationEn: For an ideal Atwood machine, $T = \frac{2m_1 m_2}{m_1 + m_2}g = \frac{2(2)(6)}{2 + 6}g = \frac{24}{8}g = 3g$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: A rocket of initial mass $M_0$ starts from rest in gravity-free space and ejects exhaust gas at a constant speed $u$ relative to the rocket. When the mass of the rocket decreases to $M_0 / e^2$, its speed is
questions.explanationEn: By Tsiolkovsky's rocket equation in free space, $v = u\ln\left(\frac{M_0}{M}\right)$. Substituting $M = M_0/e^2$ gives $v = u\ln(e^2) = 2u$. Hence, option (D) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: For an ideal three-dimensional gas of non-relativistic bosons of mass $m$ and number density $n$, the Bose-Einstein condensation temperature $T_c$ scales with $m$ and $n$ as:
questions.explanationEn: BEC occurs when the thermal de Broglie wavelength $\lambda_T = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2\pi m k_B T}}$ satisfies $n\lambda_T^3 = \zeta(3/2) \approx 2.612$. Solving for $T_c$ gives $T_c = \frac{2\pi\hbar^2}{m k_B}\left(\frac{n}{\zeta(3/2)}\right)^{2/3} \propto m^{-1} n^{2/3}$. Hence, option (D) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: In a Zener diode voltage regulator, an unregulated DC source of $18\text{ V}$ is connected through a series resistor $R_s = 200\ \Omega$ to an ideal reverse-biased Zener diode ($V_Z = 12\text{ V}$) in parallel with a variable load resistor $R_L$. The minimum value of $R_L$ for which the output voltage remains regulated at $12\text{ V}$ is:
questions.explanationEn: Regulation is maintained as long as the open-circuit voltage across $R_L$ (with the Zener removed) is at least $V_Z$, i.e., $I_Z \ge 0$. At the threshold $I_Z = 0$, $V_s \frac{R_{L,\min}}{R_s + R_{L,\min}} = V_Z \implies 18 \frac{R_{L,\min}}{200 + R_{L,\min}} = 12 \implies 3 R_{L,\min} = 2(200 + R_{L,\min}) \implies R_{L,\min} = 400\ \Omega$. Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.questionTextEn: Inside a uniform solid sphere of mass density $\rho$ and radius $R$, a spherical cavity of radius $R/2$ is scooped out with its center displaced by a vector $\vec{d}$ from the center of the original sphere. The gravitational field $\vec{g}$ at any point inside the cavity is
optionsEn: radially directed toward the center of the cavity with magnitude $\frac{4}{3}\pi G\rho r$
questions.explanationEn: By superposition, the sphere with a cavity is the sum of a complete sphere of density $+\rho$ centered at $O$ and a smaller sphere of density $-\rho$ centered at $\vec{d}$. At position $\vec{r}$ inside the cavity, $\vec{g}(\vec{r}) = -\frac{4}{3}\pi G\rho\vec{r} + \frac{4}{3}\pi G\rho(\vec{r} - \vec{d}) = -\frac{4}{3}\pi G\rho\,\vec{d}$, which is completely uniform. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: A free particle of mass $m$ in one dimension has the wavefunction $\psi(x) = A e^{ikx} + B e^{-ikx}$, where $A$, $B$ are complex constants and $k > 0$ is real. The probability current density $J$ is:
questions.explanationEn: Using $J = \frac{\hbar}{m}\operatorname{Im}(\psi^* \frac{d\psi}{dx})$: $\psi^* \frac{d\psi}{dx} = (A^* e^{-ikx} + B^* e^{ikx})(ik A e^{ikx} - ik B e^{-ikx}) = ik(|A|^2 - |B|^2) + ik(B^* A e^{2ikx} - A^* B e^{-2ikx})$. Notice $B^* A e^{2ikx} - (B^* A e^{2ikx})^*$ is purely imaginary, so multiplying by $i$ makes it purely real! Its imaginary part vanishes, leaving $J = \frac{\hbar k}{m}(|A|^2 - |B|^2)$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: In a circuit, a $12\text{ V}$ ideal battery is connected through a switch to a series resistor $R_1 = 4\ \Omega$, which feeds a parallel combination of a resistor $R_2 = 6\ \Omega$ and an ideal inductor $L = 2\text{ H}$. Immediately after the switch is closed ($t = 0^+$) and in the steady state ($t \to \infty$), the current drawn from the battery is, respectively,
questions.explanationEn: At $t = 0^+$, the inductor acts as an open circuit ($I_L = 0$), so $I(0^+) = \frac{12}{R_1 + R_2} = \frac{12}{10} = 1.2\text{ A}$. As $t \to \infty$, the ideal inductor acts as a short circuit bypassing $R_2$, so $I(\infty) = \frac{12}{R_1} = \frac{12}{4} = 3.0\text{ A}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A small block rests on the smooth inclined face of a wedge of angle $\theta$. The horizontal acceleration $a$ that must be imparted to the wedge so that the block remains stationary relative to the wedge is
questions.explanationEn: In the accelerating frame of the wedge, a horizontal pseudo-force $ma$ acts opposite to $\vec{a}$. Balancing forces parallel to the incline gives $mg\sin\theta = ma\cos\theta \implies a = g\tan\theta$. Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: A particle in a 1D infinite square well with energy eigenvalues $E_n = n^2 E_1$ is in the normalized state $\psi(x) = \frac{3}{5}\psi_1(x) + \frac{4}{5}\psi_3(x)$. The expectation value of its energy $\langle E \rangle$ is:
questions.explanationEn: The probabilities of measuring $E_1$ and $E_3 = 9E_1$ are $\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{25}$ and $\left(\frac{4}{5}\right)^2 = \frac{16}{25}$, respectively. Thus $\langle E \rangle = \frac{9}{25}E_1 + \frac{16}{25}(9E_1) = \frac{153}{25}E_1$. Hence, option (D) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: A $3 \times 3$ matrix $A$ has eigenvalues $1$, $-1$, and $2$. The trace of the matrix $A^4 + 2A^2$ is
questions.explanationEn: The eigenvalues of $B = A^4 + 2A^2$ are $\mu_i = \lambda_i^4 + 2\lambda_i^2$. For $\lambda = 1$: $1 + 2 = 3$; for $\lambda = -1$: $1 + 2 = 3$; for $\lambda = 2$: $16 + 8 = 24$. Therefore, $\text{Tr}(A^4 + 2A^2) = 3 + 3 + 24 = 30$. Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: The Taylor series expansion of $f(x) = \ln(\cos x)$ about $x = 0$, up to the term of order $x^4$, is
questions.explanationEn: Write $\cos x = 1 - \frac{x^2}{2} + \frac{x^4}{24} + O(x^6) = 1 + u$, where $u = -\frac{x^2}{2} + \frac{x^4}{24}$. Using $\ln(1 + u) = u - \frac{u^2}{2} + O(u^3)$ gives $\ln(\cos x) = \left(-\frac{x^2}{2} + \frac{x^4}{24}\right) - \frac{1}{2}\left(-\frac{x^2}{2}\right)^2 + O(x^6) = -\frac{x^2}{2} - \frac{x^4}{12} + O(x^6)$. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Consider a logic circuit made of four $2$-input NOR gates: Gate $1$ takes inputs $A$ and $B$ to produce $P$; Gate $2$ takes $A$ and $P$ to produce $Q$; Gate $3$ takes $B$ and $P$ to produce $R$; and Gate $4$ takes $Q$ and $R$ to produce the final output $Y$. The circuit is equivalent to a $2$-input:
questions.explanationEn: Evaluate each gate: $P = \overline{A + B}$, $Q = \overline{A + P} = \bar{A}(A+B) = \bar{A}B$, and $R = \overline{B + P} = \bar{B}(A+B) = A\bar{B}$. Finally, Gate $4$ computes $Y = \overline{Q + R} = \overline{\bar{A}B + A\bar{B}} = \overline{A \oplus B}$, which is a $2$-input XNOR gate. Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.questionTextEn: For a non-interacting gas of spin-$1/2$ fermions in $d$ spatial dimensions with number density $n = N / L^d$, the Fermi energy $E_F$ at $T = 0\text{ K}$ scales with $n$ as:
questions.explanationEn: At $T = 0$, the number of states up to Fermi wavevector $k_F$ in $d$ dimensions scales as $N \propto L^d k_F^d$, so $k_F \propto (N/L^d)^{1/d} = n^{1/d}$. Since $E_F = \frac{\hbar^2 k_F^2}{2m}$, we obtain $E_F \propto k_F^2 \propto n^{2/d}$. Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: A thin circular ring of radius $R$ carries a uniformly distributed charge $Q$. Along the symmetry axis perpendicular to the plane of the ring, the magnitude of the electric field reaches its maximum value at a distance from the center equal to
questions.explanationEn: The axial field is $E(z) = \frac{Qz}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 (z^2 + R^2)^{3/2}}$. Setting $\frac{dE}{dz} = 0$ gives $(z^2 + R^2) - 3z^2 = 0 \implies 2z^2 = R^2 \implies z = \frac{R}{\sqrt{2}}$.

questions.questionTextEn: For a three-dimensional classical ideal gas in thermal equilibrium at temperature $T$, the most probable translational kinetic energy $E_{\text{mp}}$ of a molecule (where the energy distribution $P(E)$ peaks) is:
questions.explanationEn: Converting the Maxwell-Boltzmann speed distribution to kinetic energy $E = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$ gives $P(E) = \frac{2}{\sqrt{\pi}(k_B T)^{3/2}} E^{1/2} e^{-E/(k_B T)}$. Setting $\frac{dP}{dE} = 0$ yields $\frac{1}{2}E^{-1/2} - \frac{1}{k_B T}E^{1/2} = 0 \implies E_{\text{mp}} = \frac{1}{2}k_B T$. (Note this differs from $\frac{1}{2}m v_{\text{mp}}^2 = k_B T$ because of the Jacobian $dv/dE$.) Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: The system of linear equations $x + y + z = 1$, $x + 2y + 3z = 2$, and $x + 3y + kz = 4$ has NO solution when $k$ is equal to
questions.explanationEn: Subtracting the first equation from the second and third gives $y + 2z = 1$ and $2y + (k - 1)z = 3$. Subtracting twice the former from the latter yields $(k - 5)z = 1$. When $k = 5$, this becomes $0 \cdot z = 1$, which is inconsistent and has no solution. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda$ is incident from air onto a soap film of refractive index $n = \frac{4}{3}$ at an angle of incidence $i$ such that $\sin i = \frac{4}{5}$. The minimum non-zero thickness of the film for which it appears completely dark in reflected light is
questions.explanationEn: By Snell's law, $\sin r = \frac{\sin i}{n} = \frac{4/5}{4/3} = \frac{3}{5}$, so $\cos r = \frac{4}{5}$. For a soap film in air, destructive interference in reflection occurs at $2nt\cos r = m\lambda$. For the minimum non-zero thickness ($m = 1$), $t = \frac{\lambda}{2(4/3)(4/5)} = \frac{15\lambda}{32}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A vertically polarized light beam passes normally through a half-wave plate whose fast axis is oriented at $35^\circ$ clockwise from the vertical. The emergent beam is linearly polarized at an angle (measured clockwise from the vertical) of
questions.explanationEn: A half-wave plate reflects the linear polarization direction across its fast axis. If the incident polarization makes angle $\theta = 35^\circ$ with the fast axis, the emergent polarization is rotated by $2\theta = 70^\circ$ from the vertical.

questions.questionTextEn: For a three-dimensional isotropic quantum harmonic oscillator with energy levels $E_N = \left(N + \frac{3}{2}\right)\hbar\omega$ ($N = n_x + n_y + n_z$), the degeneracy of the $N = 3$ energy level is:
questions.explanationEn: The number of non-negative integer triples $(n_x, n_y, n_z)$ summing to $N$ is $g_N = \frac{(N + 1)(N + 2)}{2}$. For $N = 3$, $g_3 = \frac{4 \times 5}{2} = 10$. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Consider a semiconductor with both electrons (concentration $n$, mobility $\mu_e$) and holes (concentration $p$, mobility $\mu_h$) contributing to transport. The net Hall coefficient $R_H$ vanishes when:
questions.explanationEn: For a two-carrier semiconductor, the Hall coefficient is $R_H = \frac{p \mu_h^2 - n \mu_e^2}{e(p \mu_h + n \mu_e)^2}$. Setting the numerator to zero gives $R_H = 0$ when $n \mu_e^2 = p \mu_h^2$. (Note that $n = p$ does not give $R_H = 0$ unless $\mu_e = \mu_h$.) Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.questionTextEn: A uniform cubical block of density $0.8\text{ g/cm}^3$ floats in water (density $1.0\text{ g/cm}^3$). Oil of density $0.6\text{ g/cm}^3$ (immiscible with water) is slowly poured on top of the water until the oil completely covers the top surface of the block. The fraction of the block's volume now submerged in water is
questions.explanationEn: Let $f$ be the fraction of volume in water and $(1 - f)$ in oil. By Archimedes' principle, $\rho_b = f\rho_w + (1 - f)\rho_o \implies 0.8 = 1.0f + 0.6(1 - f) = 0.6 + 0.4f \implies f = 0.50$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Two concentric thin conducting spherical shells of radii $R$ and $3R$ form a spherical capacitor in vacuum. Its capacitance is
questions.explanationEn: For a spherical capacitor of inner radius $a = R$ and outer radius $b = 3R$, $C = \frac{4\pi\varepsilon_0 a b}{b - a} = \frac{4\pi\varepsilon_0 (3R^2)}{2R} = 6\pi\varepsilon_0 R$.

questions.questionTextEn: Consider the pair of functions $y_1(x) = e^{2x}$ and $y_2(x) = e^{-3x}$ on $\mathbb{R}$. Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
optionsEn: Both $y_1$ and $y_2$ satisfy the ODE $y'' + y' - 6y = 0$
Their Wronskian is constant for all $x$
questions.explanationEn: Computing the Wronskian: $W(x) = y_1 y_2' - y_1' y_2 = e^{2x}(-3e^{-3x}) - (2e^{2x})e^{-3x} = -5e^{-x} \neq 0$ (A and D are true, D is false). The characteristic equation with roots $2$ and $-3$ is $(r - 2)(r + 3) = r^2 + r - 6 = 0$, corresponding to $y'' + y' - 6y = 0$ (C is true). Hence, options (A), (B), and (D) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: For a system of $N$ particles with total mass $M$, center-of-mass position $\vec{R}_{\text{cm}}$, and center-of-mass velocity $\vec{V}_{\text{cm}}$, which of the following statement(s) is/are ALWAYS true?
optionsEn: Internal forces can never change the total kinetic energy of the system
The total kinetic energy equals $K = \frac{1}{2}M V_{\text{cm}}^2 + K_{\text{rel}}$, where $K_{\text{rel}}$ is the kinetic energy measured in the center-of-mass frame
The internal forces between particles do not contribute to the acceleration of the center of mass
The total angular momentum about the origin equals $\vec{L} = \vec{R}_{\text{cm}} \times M\vec{V}_{\text{cm}} + \vec{L}_{\text{cm}}$
questions.explanationEn: (B) König's theorem for kinetic energy holds generally. (D) König's theorem for angular momentum holds generally. (C) By Newton's third law, internal forces cancel in pairs in $M\vec{A}_{\text{cm}} = \vec{F}_{\text{ext}}$. (A) False: Internal forces (e.g., an explosion or releasing a compressed spring between two blocks) can change $K_{\text{rel}}$ and hence the total kinetic energy. Hence, options (B), (C), and (D) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: A sound source emits frequency $f_0$ in still air (sound speed $c_s$). Consider two cases with speed $v < c_s$: Case I—source approaches a stationary observer at speed $v$; Case II—observer approaches a stationary source at speed $v$. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
optionsEn: In the limit $v \ll c_s$, both cases give the same first-order frequency shift $\Delta f \approx f_0 \frac{v}{c_s}$
The wavelength in air between source and observer is shorter than $c_s / f_0$ in Case I, but remains $c_s / f_0$ in Case II
The observed frequency in Case I is strictly greater than that in Case II
The observed frequencies in Case I and Case II are identical for all $v < c_s$
questions.explanationEn: In Case I, $f_{\text{I}} = \frac{f_0}{1 - v/c_s} = f_0(1 + v/c_s + v^2/c_s^2 + \dots)$ and $\lambda_{\text{I}} = (c_s - v)/f_0$. In Case II, $f_{\text{II}} = f_0(1 + v/c_s)$ and $\lambda_{\text{II}} = c_s/f_0$. Thus $f_{\text{I}} > f_{\text{II}}$ for $0 < v < c_s$, while both match to first order in $v/c_s$.

questions.questionTextEn: Consider ideal Op-Amp circuits operating in the linear region with negative feedback. Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
optionsEn: A unity-gain voltage follower (output directly shorted to the inverting terminal, input at the non-inverting terminal) has $V_o = V_{\text{in}}$ and very high input impedance
In an inverting amplifier with input resistor $R_1$ and feedback resistor $R_f$, the effective input impedance seen by the voltage source is $R_1$
In a non-inverting amplifier with ground resistor $R_1$ and feedback resistor $R_f$, the closed-loop voltage gain is always greater than or equal to $1$
The virtual short condition ($V_+ = V_-$) holds even when the Op-Amp is operated with positive feedback alone (e.g., a Schmitt trigger)
questions.explanationEn: (A) Voltage follower has $V_- = V_o = V_+ = V_{\text{in}}$ and ideal $Z_{\text{in}} = \infty$ (True). (B) Because $V_- = 0$ (virtual ground), the input source sees resistor $R_1$ connected to virtual ground, so $Z_{\text{in}} = R_1$ (True). (C) $A_v = 1 + \frac{R_f}{R_1} \ge 1$ for $R_f, R_1 \ge 0$ (True). (D) Virtual short holds only with negative feedback in the linear region; positive feedback drives the Op-Amp into saturation (False). Hence, options (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Let $\vec{a}_1, \vec{a}_2, \vec{a}_3$ be the primitive translation vectors of a 3D direct Bravais lattice (primitive cell volume $V_c$) and $\vec{b}_1, \vec{b}_2, \vec{b}_3$ be the corresponding reciprocal lattice primitive vectors (with the $2\pi$ convention). Which of the following statement(s) is/are always correct?
optionsEn: The volume of the primitive cell of the reciprocal lattice is $\frac{(2\pi)^3}{V_c}$
Every reciprocal lattice vector $\vec{G}_{hkl} = h\vec{b}_1 + k\vec{b}_2 + l\vec{b}_3$ is perpendicular to the crystal plane $(hkl)$
For any direct lattice vector $\vec{R}$ and reciprocal lattice vector $\vec{G}$, $e^{i\vec{G}\cdot\vec{R}} = -1$
questions.explanationEn: (A) By definition of the reciprocal basis, $\vec{a}_i \cdot \vec{b}_j = 2\pi\delta_{ij}$ (True). (B) The reciprocal primitive cell volume is $|\vec{b}_1 \cdot (\vec{b}_2 \times \vec{b}_3)| = \frac{(2\pi)^3}{V_c}$ (True). (C) $\vec{G}_{hkl}$ is orthogonal to any two vectors lying in the $(hkl)$ plane, so it is normal to the $(hkl)$ plane (True). (D) Since $\vec{G}\cdot\vec{R} = 2\pi \times (\text{integer})$, we have $e^{i\vec{G}\cdot\vec{R}} = +1$, not $-1$ (False). Hence, options (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: For an equilibrium photon gas (blackbody radiation) inside a cavity of volume $V$ at temperature $T$ with internal energy $U = a V T^4$, which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE?
optionsEn: The Helmholtz free energy is $F = -\frac{1}{3}a V T^4$
The Gibbs free energy $G$ is identically zero
The chemical potential $\mu$ of photons is zero
The heat capacity at constant volume is $C_V = 4a V T^3$
questions.explanationEn: For a photon gas: $U = aVT^4$, $P = \frac{1}{3}aT^4$, $S = \frac{4}{3}aVT^3$. Thus $F = U - TS = -\frac{1}{3}aVT^4$ (A True); $G = F + PV = -\frac{1}{3}aVT^4 + \frac{1}{3}aVT^4 = 0$ (B True); since $G = \mu N = 0$ (photon number is not conserved), $\mu = 0$ (C True); and $C_V = (\partial U/\partial T)_V = 4aVT^3$ (D True). Hence, (A), (B), (C), and (D) are all correct.

questions.questionTextEn: In the Bohr model of the hydrogen atom ($Z = 1$), as the principal quantum number $n$ increases, which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE?
optionsEn: The orbital speed $v_n$ of the electron decreases as $1/n$
The orbital time period $T_n$ increases as $n^3$
The magnitude of the potential energy is always twice the kinetic energy ($|U_n| = 2K_n$)
The angular momentum of the electron decreases as $1/n$
questions.explanationEn: In the Bohr atom: $r_n \propto n^2$ and $v_n \propto 1/n$ (A True); $T_n = \frac{2\pi r_n}{v_n} \propto n^3$ (B True); by the virial theorem for the Coulomb potential, $U_n = -2K_n \implies |U_n| = 2K_n$ (C True); and $L_n = n\hbar$ increases linearly with $n$ (D False). Hence, (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Two particles of masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ undergo a one-dimensional head-on elastic collision. Which of the following statement(s) is/are ALWAYS correct?
optionsEn: If $m_1 = m_2$, the two particles exchange their velocities
The relative speed of separation after collision equals the relative speed of approach before collision
Both particles always reverse their directions of motion after collision
questions.explanationEn: In a 1D elastic collision, $e = \frac{v_2' - v_1'}{v_1 - v_2} = 1$ (A and B are true). When $m_1 = m_2$, $v_1' = v_2$ and $v_2' = v_1$ (B is true). (D) False: For instance, a heavy mass hitting a light stationary mass continues moving forward. Hence, options (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: At a planar interface separating two linear magnetic media of permeabilities $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ carrying a free surface current density $\vec{K}_f$, which of the following boundary conditions is/are always valid?
optionsEn: If $\vec{K}_f \neq \vec{0}$, $\hat{n}\times(\vec{H}_2 - \vec{H}_1) = \vec{K}_f$, where $\hat{n}$ points from medium $1$ into medium $2$
If $\vec{K}_f = \vec{0}$, the tangential component of $\vec{H}$ is continuous across the interface ($H_{1\parallel} = H_{2\parallel}$)

questions.questionTextEn: A point charge $+q$ is placed at $(0, 0, d)$ above an infinite grounded conducting plane at $z = 0$. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
optionsEn: The potential in the region $z > 0$ is identical to that of $+q$ at $(0, 0, d)$ and an image charge $-q$ at $(0, 0, -d)$
The induced surface charge density on the plane at distance $\rho$ from the origin is $\sigma(\rho) = -\frac{qd}{2\pi(\rho^2 + d^2)^{3/2}}$
The total electrostatic work required to bring $+q$ from infinity to $(0, 0, d)$ is $-\frac{q^2}{8\pi\varepsilon_0 d}$
The total induced charge integrated over the entire $z = 0$ plane is $-q$
questions.explanationEn: The image charge $-q$ at $(0,0,-d)$ yields $V = 0$ on $z = 0$ and gives $\sigma(\rho) = -\varepsilon_0 \left.\frac{\partial V}{\partial z}\right|_{z=0^+} = -\frac{qd}{2\pi(\rho^2+d^2)^{3/2}}$, whose integral over the plane is $-q$ (first three True). The work to assemble the system (field exists only in $z > 0$) is half the two-charge interaction energy: $W = \frac{1}{2}\left(-\frac{q^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0(2d)}\right) = -\frac{q^2}{16\pi\varepsilon_0 d}$, not $-\frac{q^2}{8\pi\varepsilon_0 d}$ (False).

questions.questionTextEn: The value of the limit $\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{1 - \cos(4x)}{x^2}$ is ____. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: Using $1 - \cos(4x) = 2\sin^2(2x)$, we get $\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{2\sin^2(2x)}{x^2} = 8\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\frac{\sin 2x}{2x}\right)^2 = 8$.

questions.questionTextEn: In a cubic crystal, the acute angle between the crystallographic directions $[110]$ and $[111]$ is ______ degrees. (Rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.explanationEn: In a cubic lattice, the angle $\phi$ between directions $[u_1 v_1 w_1]$ and $[u_2 v_2 w_2]$ is given by $\cos\phi = \frac{u_1 u_2 + v_1 v_2 + w_1 w_2}{\sqrt{u_1^2+v_1^2+w_1^2}\sqrt{u_2^2+v_2^2+w_2^2}}$. For $[110]$ and $[111]$: $\cos\phi = \frac{1(1)+1(1)+0(1)}{\sqrt{2}\sqrt{3}} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{6}} = \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}} \approx 0.8165$, giving $\phi \approx 35.26^\circ$.

questions.questionTextEn: A particle moves along the $x$-axis from $x = 0$ to $x = 2\text{ m}$ under the action of a force $F(x) = (3x^2 + 2x)\text{ N}$. The work done by the force, in $\text{J}$, is ____. (Answer in integer)

Two moles of an ideal rigid diatomic gas are heated isobarically from $300\text{ K}$ to $400\text{ K}$. Taking $R = 8.314\text{ J/(mol}\cdot\text{K)}$, the heat absorbed by the gas is ______ $\text{kJ}$ (Round off to 2 decimal places).
questions.explanationEn: For a rigid diatomic gas, $C_P = \frac{7}{2}R$. Thus $Q = n C_P \Delta T = 2 \times 3.5 \times 8.314 \times 100 = 5819.8\text{ J} \approx 5.82\text{ kJ}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Taking the Compton wavelength of an electron as $\lambda_C = 0.02426\text{ \AA}$, the Compton wavelength shift of an X-ray photon scattered at $60^\circ$ off a stationary free electron is ______ $\text{\AA}$ (Round off to 4 decimal places).
questions.explanationEn: The Compton shift is $\Delta\lambda = \lambda_C(1 - \cos 60^\circ) = 0.02426(1 - 0.5) = 0.01213\text{ \AA} \approx 0.0121\text{ \AA}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A long straight wire carries a steady current of $15\text{ A}$. Taking $\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T}\cdot\text{m/A}$, the magnitude of the magnetic field at a perpendicular distance of $3\text{ cm}$ from the wire is ______ $\mu\text{T}$. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: Using $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r} = \frac{2 \times 10^{-7} \times 15}{0.03} = 1.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ T} = 100\ \mu\text{T}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Three particles of masses $2\text{ kg}$, $3\text{ kg}$, and $5\text{ kg}$ are located along the $x$-axis at $x = 1\text{ m}$, $x = 4\text{ m}$, and $x = 6\text{ m}$, respectively. The $x$-coordinate of their center of mass, in $\text{m}$, is ____. (Rounded off to one decimal place)

A $4\ \mu\text{F}$ capacitor charged to $100\text{ V}$ is disconnected from the battery and connected in parallel to an identical uncharged $4\ \mu\text{F}$ capacitor. The electrostatic energy lost as heat and radiation during charge redistribution is ______ $\text{mJ}$. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: The energy lost is $\Delta U = \frac{1}{2}\frac{C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2}(V_1 - V_2)^2 = \frac{1}{2}(2 \times 10^{-6})(100)^2 = 10 \times 10^{-3}\text{ J} = 10\text{ mJ}$.

questions.questionTextEn: In a Zener voltage regulator, a $24\text{ V}$ DC supply feeds a $400\ \Omega$ series resistor connected to an ideal $12\text{ V}$ Zener diode in parallel with a $600\ \Omega$ load resistor. The current flowing through the Zener diode is ______ $\text{mA}$. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: Without the Zener diode, the voltage across the $600\ \Omega$ load would be $24 \times \frac{600}{400+600} = 14.4\text{ V} > 12\text{ V}$, so the Zener is in breakdown and clamps the output at $12\text{ V}$. The source current is $I_s = \frac{24 - 12}{400} = 30\text{ mA}$ and the load current is $I_L = \frac{12}{600} = 20\text{ mA}$. Thus, $I_Z = I_s - I_L = 30 - 20 = 10\text{ mA}$.

questions.questionTextEn: When the movable mirror of a Michelson interferometer is displaced by $0.06\text{ mm}$, exactly $200$ fringes cross the reference crosshair. The wavelength of the monochromatic light used is ______ $\text{nm}$. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: Using $2d = N\lambda$, we obtain $\lambda = \frac{2 \times 0.06 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}}{200} = 6.0 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m} = 600\text{ nm}$.

questions.questionTextEn: An abrupt one-sided $p^+$-$n$ silicon junction ($N_a \gg N_d$) has donor concentration $N_d = 1.0 \times 10^{21}\text{ m}^{-3}$ and built-in potential $V_0 = 0.7\text{ V}$. Taking relative permittivity $\varepsilon_r = 12$, $\varepsilon_0 = 8.85 \times 10^{-12}\text{ F/m}$, and $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$, the depletion width $W$ at a reverse bias voltage $V_R = 7.3\text{ V}$ is ______ $\mu\text{m}$. (Rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.explanationEn: For a one-sided $p^+$-$n$ junction ($N_a \gg N_d$), the depletion width lies almost entirely on the $n$-side: $W \approx \sqrt{\frac{2\varepsilon_r \varepsilon_0 (V_0 + V_R)}{e N_d}}$. Substituting $\varepsilon_r \varepsilon_0 = 12 \times 8.85 \times 10^{-12} = 1.062 \times 10^{-10}\text{ F/m}$ and $V_0 + V_R = 8.0\text{ V}$ gives $W = \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 1.062 \times 10^{-10} \times 8.0}{1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 1.0 \times 10^{21}}} = \sqrt{1.062 \times 10^{-11}}\text{ m} \approx 3.26\ \mu\text{m}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A spherical soap bubble of surface tension $0.035\text{ N/m}$ is blown isothermally so that its radius increases from $2\text{ cm}$ to $5\text{ cm}$. The work done against surface tension, in $\text{mJ}$, is ____. (Rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.explanationEn: Since a soap bubble has two free surfaces, $W = 2T \cdot 4\pi(R_2^2 - R_1^2) = 8\pi(0.035)(0.05^2 - 0.02^2) = 8\pi(0.035)(2.1 \times 10^{-3}) \approx 1.85 \times 10^{-3}\text{ J} = 1.85\text{ mJ}$.

questions.questionTextEn: In a Fresnel biprism experiment, the distance between the slit and the eyepiece is $1.5\text{ m}$ and the fringe width is $1.45\text{ mm}$. A convex lens placed between the biprism and the eyepiece produces sharp images of the two virtual coherent sources at two conjugate positions with measured separations $0.90\text{ mm}$ and $0.40\text{ mm}$. The wavelength of the light used is ______ $\text{nm}$. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: By the displacement method, the separation between the virtual coherent sources is $d = \sqrt{d_1 d_2} = \sqrt{0.90 \times 0.40} = 0.60\text{ mm}$. Hence $\lambda = \frac{\beta d}{D} = \frac{1.45 \times 10^{-3} \times 0.60 \times 10^{-3}}{1.5} = 5.8 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m} = 580\text{ nm}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A 1D quantum harmonic oscillator is in the normalized state $|\psi\rangle = \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}|0\rangle + \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}|2\rangle$. The standard deviation (uncertainty) in its energy is $\alpha\hbar\omega$, where $\alpha$ is ______ (Round off to 2 decimal places).
questions.explanationEn: For a two-eigenstate superposition, $\Delta E = |c_0 c_2||E_2 - E_0|$. Here $E_2 - E_0 = \left(\frac{5}{2} - \frac{1}{2}\right)\hbar\omega = 2\hbar\omega$, so $\Delta E = \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\cdot\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\right)(2\hbar\omega) = \frac{4}{5}\hbar\omega = 0.80\hbar\omega$.

questions.questionTextEn: Evaluate the shifted Gaussian integral $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{-(x^2 - 2x)}\,dx$: its numerical value is ____. (Rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.explanationEn: Completing the square in the exponent gives $-(x^2 - 2x) = 1 - (x - 1)^2$. Thus $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{-(x^2 - 2x)}\,dx = e \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{-(x - 1)^2}\,dx = e\sqrt{\pi} \approx 2.7183 \times 1.7725 \approx 4.82$.

questions.questionTextEn: Taking Earth's radius as $R = 6400\text{ km}$ and $g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$, the Earth's rotation period (in minutes) at which an object at the equator would become completely weightless is ____. (Rounded off to one decimal place)
questions.explanationEn: Weightlessness at the equator occurs when $\omega^2 R = g \implies T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{R}{g}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{6.4 \times 10^6}{9.8}} \approx 5077.6\text{ s} \approx 84.6\text{ minutes}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A thin circular disc of radius $R = 3\text{ m}$ carries a uniform surface charge density $\sigma$. Taking the electrostatic potential to be zero at infinity, the ratio of the potential on the axis at $z = 4\text{ m}$ to the potential at the center of the disc ($z = 0$) is ______. (Round off to 2 decimal places)
questions.explanationEn: Along the symmetry axis of a uniformly charged disc, $V(z) = \frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}\left(\sqrt{R^2 + z^2} - z\right)$. At $z = 0$, $V(0) = \frac{\sigma R}{2\varepsilon_0}$. Hence $\frac{V(4)}{V(0)} = \frac{\sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} - 4}{3} = \frac{5 - 4}{3} = \frac{1}{3} \approx 0.33$.

questions.questionTextEn: If $(121)_b = (64)_{10}$, where $b$ is a positive integer base, the value of $b$ is ______. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: Expanding $(121)_b$ in decimal gives $b^2 + 2b + 1 = 64 \implies (b + 1)^2 = 64$. Since $b > 0$, $b + 1 = 8 \implies b = 7$.

questions.questionTextEn: A rectangular coil of $20$ turns with dimensions $10\text{ cm} \times 15\text{ cm}$ carries a steady current of $4\text{ A}$ in a uniform magnetic field of $0.5\text{ T}$. When the plane of the coil makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with the magnetic field direction, the magnitude of the torque on the coil is ______ $\text{N}\cdot\text{m}$. (Round off to 2 decimal places)
questions.explanationEn: The angle between the area normal $\hat{n}$ and $\vec{B}$ is $\theta = 90^\circ - 30^\circ = 60^\circ$. Thus $\tau = N I A B \sin 60^\circ = 20(4)(0.015)(0.5)\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 0.3\sqrt{3} \approx 0.52\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A reversible Carnot heat engine operating between $600\text{ K}$ and $300\text{ K}$ uses all of its work output to drive a reversible Carnot refrigerator operating between $250\text{ K}$ and $300\text{ K}$. For every $100\text{ J}$ of heat absorbed by the engine from the $600\text{ K}$ reservoir, the heat extracted by the refrigerator from the $250\text{ K}$ reservoir is ______ $\text{J}$ (Answer in integer).
questions.explanationEn: The engine efficiency is $\eta = 1 - \frac{300}{600} = 0.5$, so it produces work $W = 0.5 \times 100 = 50\text{ J}$. The refrigerator has $\text{COP} = \frac{250}{300 - 250} = 5$, so it extracts $Q_{\text{cold}} = \text{COP} \times W = 5 \times 50 = 250\text{ J}$.
